findings.title: The lifetime test does not falsify missing retention integration in real run operations
findings.affected_claim: Genuine active run operations preserve checked-record identity and work reuse while completed operations release both owner roots.
findings.violated_property: Selected TASK.r04 requires genuine owner construction and active identity/work reuse; Product REQ-R-ABG3-INTERPRET-013 and STDO EVALUATION section 3 keep component evidence distinct from integrated behavior.
findings.observation: Three actual completed installed calls assert only zero after completion. Positive row retention, identity reuse and overlap are tested by manually calling retainExecutionBasisLifetime after those calls completed. No assertion sees a positive retained row/body while a real run owner is in flight. The body-root positive assertion also permits zero historyBasisBodies.
findings.counterexample: Static mutation thought experiment, NOT executed: omit the four yield* retainBasisLifetime calls in runInvocationOwner/runCurrentIntentOwner/runSelectedActionOwner/runPendingExecutionOwner. Completed calls still leave all gauges at ZERO, and every positive/manual probe still opens its own handles. These assertions therefore do not reject loss of the production integration and its active reuse. Actual execution under that mutation remains unperformed.
findings.causal_assessment: The test substitutes direct helper acquisition for the owner acquisition at the positive observation seam. Zero-only postconditions cannot distinguish successful acquisition-and-release from no acquisition.
findings.confidence: The assertion dependency is directly visible in source; no numerical likelihood or mutation pass is claimed.
findings.blast_radius: Proof of active reuse for all four owner entry families; does not establish a defect in their current source or ordinary output semantics. Completed-call release observations retain their bounded meaning.
findings.workaround_or_containment: Keep active integrated reuse unproved until an independently authorized frozen proof observes positive gauges and repeated-row identity/work inside an actual owner operation, then zero at exit. Existing external proof can supply this evidence without changing Product source.
findings.repair_complexity: Bounded proof instrumentation/fixture work; exact cost indeterminate until the existing leaf/owner observation seam is selected. No runtime redesign is evidenced.
findings.regression_risk: Proof-only external observation is low runtime risk; introducing fixture-authored invocation or event truth would invalidate the intended evidence.

causal_trace: Root admission execution_basis.ts:2080-2156 places admitted invocationRef and complete rawInputValue in basis_admitted; child :2623 inherits invocationRef; continuation :2757-2794 retains original source body.

Execution-basis projection preserves full output, raw admission/digests and final identity checks. Per-cut exact match/cardinality occurs before cache lookup (calculus/execution_basis_record.ts:104-160). Refusals remain cold.

Owned event-prefix authentication reaches actual store RuntimeHistory; copied/raw/validation prefixes cannot reuse checked-row retention. retainExecutionBasisLifetime resolves only active exact coordinate ownership.

RuntimeHistory checked-row facts key generation plus eventId/ordinal under invocation holds; committed decoded basis bodies are retained only for that held invocation. Logical byte metrics are computed at insertion; observations sum recorded counts rather than serializing rows.

All four run owner entry families use Effect.scoped/acquireRelease. Start holds the called invocation; three continuation families hold prepared/original invocation after source selection. Children share the existing admitted invocation relation.

Finalizers release on result/refusal/failure/defect/interruption/nonterminal exits without semantic closure. Borrowed completion preserves physical session while scoped release removes retention. Physical close/abandon clears all handles and roots; epoch invalidates old releases.

Transaction rollback calls RuntimeHistory.truncate, clearing roots and invalidating selection generation; append I/O catch also disposes holds. Ordinary later reads cannot open handles; caller-owned materialized/results are outside the guarantee.

Reference-counted holds preserve other active invocation entries and same-invocation overlapping handles. A continuation can retain multiple historical/child basis rows while active; no rows<=invocations or global heap bound is claimed.
